sections.html:
Mansfield lies between Fort Worth and Dallas. Its housing is mostly recent suburban construction. Owners of dated floor plans find themselves up against new builds nearby. Condition and list price end up driving the timeline more than anything else.

Population was an estimated 84,444 on July 1, 2025, up 16.3 percent from 2020. Households average 3.04 people, and showings tend to open with questions about bedrooms, yard and school zone.

Sellers here usually pick among three paths, each costing something different:

  • An agent listing exposes the house to the widest pool, along with weekend showings and repair requests after the inspection.
  • Going without an agent keeps the commission and puts all the paperwork on you.
  • A cash buyer accepts the house as is and lowers the offer to cover the work.

sections.h2: Mansfield home values and housing costs
sections.html:
Mansfield is mid-priced for North Texas. Owners occupy most homes, and people stay put: 88.2 percent of residents were at the same address a year before.

Mansfield housing costs, 2020-2024

That median is only a midpoint. A particular house can land far above or below it depending on age, size and repairs needed.

sections.h2: Which county handles your Mansfield property?
sections.html:
Mansfield spreads across three counties: mostly Tarrant, with pieces in Johnson and Ellis. Where your lot falls decides which office bills the taxes and which clerk files the deed.

  • Your deed's legal description or the county printed on the tax statement answers the question.
  • Streets near downtown fall mostly in Tarrant County. Newer growth toward the south and east crosses into Johnson and Ellis.
  • U.S. Route 287 and Texas Highway 360 serve the city, and commuters bound for Fort Worth or Dallas will want to know how near you are to each.
  • Every county runs a separate appraisal district. If you live close to a county line, confirm the right one before asking about exemptions.

The town began as Walnut Creek and incorporated on August 23, 1890. Downtown's old commercial corridor is still there, and a Historic Landmark Commission recommends sites worth preserving.

Own an older home in that area? Call the city and ask if a historic designation applies before you pick a price. It is easier to hear that now than in the middle of a contract.

sections.h2: Schools and parks buyers ask about
sections.html:
The public schools are run by Mansfield Independent School District. Families check zones first, so get the current campus assignments from the district before naming a school in your ad.

City amenities include Elmer W. Oliver Nature Park, a dog park, many athletic fields and the Walnut Creek Linear Trail. Mentioning nearby campuses and trail access in the listing saves buyers a question.

Private venues such as Hawaiian Falls, Big League Dreams and the Mansfield National Golf Course also add to the area's appeal. If your street is a short drive from any of them, say so in the description, since weekend activity is part of what families here shop for.

sections.h2: Can a Mansfield house be a short-term rental?
sections.html:
Not automatically. Residential areas do not allow stays shorter than 30 days unless the property is approved first. Listing a house online does not make the use legal.

The route to approval is rezoning to a Planned Development, and nothing guarantees a yes. Most applications take about 90 to 120 days from submittal to a final decision, passing through city staff, the Planning and Zoning Commission and then the City Council.

  • The application fee is $2,500, plus $100 per acre or part of an acre.
  • A complete application carries a parking site plan, a floor plan showing exits, proof of insurance and Hotel Occupancy Tax registration.
  • Applicants also state house rules, a cap on occupants and whether the owner will live there.

If guests have stayed in the house without approval, a compliance problem may follow it to the next owner. Anyone buying for rental income can ask the Planning Department what the address is allowed to do.

Whatever route you choose, a Mansfield closing moves through about the same stages. Seeing them laid out helps you work backward from your own deadline.

  1. Collect your deed, newest tax statement and a payoff figure if a mortgage exists.
  2. Choose between an agent, a sale on your own or a cash buyer.
  3. Once you accept an offer, a title company opens a file and looks for liens and tax balances.
  4. Resolve whatever surfaces, for example an old lien or a co-owner who has not signed.
  5. Sign the deed before a notary, and the clerk for your parcel's county records it.
  6. The loan is paid from the sale proceeds and you keep the remainder.

Retail buyers add an inspection and a lender appraisal mid-process, and either can send the price back to the table. Cash buyers typically skip both, so closing speed depends mostly on how quickly the title work clears.

sections.h2: Recording the deed and clerk fees
sections.html:
A Mansfield sale may involve the Tarrant, Johnson or Ellis county clerk, whichever covers your parcel. To record a land conveyance, the clerk wants the signature along with a notary's acknowledgment, or a sworn statement made before two witnesses.

Texas Courts' 2023 clerk manual shows $5.00 for the first page and $4.00 for every page following, and counties add records management, archive and technology fees. The total differs by county, so call the clerk with your page count.

  • The same clerk takes releases of a deed of trust and affidavits.
  • A missing grantee mailing address can cost an extra $25.
  • A few commissioners courts waive recording fees when the buyer uses certain grant programs.

Bills are collected by the county tax office rather than the appraisal district, so request your balance from the Tarrant, Johnson or Ellis office. Taxes from an earlier unpaid year stay attached to the house for the next owner, and the sale year's bill gets divided at closing.

Having the statement, deed and payoff letter ready lets you answer a buyer's or title officer's first questions the same day.

Cash sales skip repair haggling and most showings, so owners of rough houses often compare that against listing. Line up the net from each path rather than just the top offer.

If the taxes are behind, ask the tax office for the full balance including earlier years, because the title company will want that figure to clear the account at closing. Sellers who expect a quick sale should do this first, since a surprise balance is one of the common reasons a closing slips.

faqs.q: Can a Mansfield house with repairs still be sold?
faqs.a: Yes. Cash buyers purchase in present condition, whereas a retail buyer usually negotiates repairs after the inspection. Weigh the money you walk away with, not only the offer.

faqs.q: How do I know which county records my Mansfield deed?
faqs.a: Look at the legal description or tax statement. The city lies mostly in Tarrant County with parts in Johnson and Ellis, and the clerk where your parcel sits records the deed.

faqs.q: What is the median home value in Mansfield?
faqs.a: $410,700 for 2020-2024. Age, size and condition can put a given house well off that midpoint.
Mansfield Independent School District. Ask the district for current campus zones before you advertise a particular school.
Page one is $5.00 and later pages $4.00 each, with smaller add-on fees. The clerk's office quotes the current total.
